title: Interface-Controlled Phase Stability in Polymorphic HfO$_2$ Revealed by Machine-Learning Atomistic Simulations
abstractExcerpt: HfO$_2$ exhibits rich polymorphism, and competition among different phases underpins many of its functional properties. Yet bulk free-energy relations alone cannot explain phase selection at mixed-phase boundaries, where interface orientation and structural continuity constrain collective rearrangements. Here, using machine-learning atomistic simulations and a Hf-centered local phase classification scheme, we show that crystallographic interface matching redirects phase competition and accessible transformation pathways.

However, current approaches for interpreting NMR spectra rely on a comparison with static DFT reference calculations, which are inadequate for materials exhibiting fast ion dynamics such as lithium battery solid electrolytes.

title: Accurate Calculation of the Thermal Conductivity of Liquids from Molecular Dynamics Using a Heat Flux Decomposition Based Correction
abstractExcerpt: Thermal conductivity (λ ) of liquids is a critical property for numerous applications, yet classical all-atom force fields consistently overestimate it in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. This work identifies the overestimation of energies stored and transferred through bonded interactions, particularly high-frequency vibrations, as the primary cause of this inaccuracy. Using heat flux decomposition techniques, we developed a physics-informed algebraic correction model to adjust MD-predicted λ values.

title: Local Symmetry Breaking and Correlated Fluctuations in Quantum Materials from Atomistic Foundation Models
abstractExcerpt: Short-range structural distortions retained within nominally high-symmetry crystals underlie the anomalous physical properties of many advanced materials. These distortions reflect local symmetry breaking and correlated fluctuations extending over nanometer length scales and picosecond timescales, making their accurate modeling challenging. Here, we demonstrate that such distortions can be modeled using a machine learning-based framework, taking RuP, the parent compound of ruthenium-pnictide superconductors, as a representative quantum material.

title: AutoSolvate 2.0: Automated Preparation of Chemically Diverse Explicit-Solvent Systems for Multiscale Molecular Simulation
abstractExcerpt: Advanced quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM), machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), and hybrid methods provide powerful engines for modeling solution-phase chemistry. Yet before production begins, chemically diverse explicit-solvent systems must be parameterized, assembled at the desired composition, relaxed, equilibrated, and sampled. This preparatory “first mile” remains labor-intensive, requiring multiple software packages and manual customization, particularly for transition-metal complexes, solvent mixtures, and multicomponent electrolytes.

title: From Field Spectra to Shared Knowledge: Harmonizing Hyperspectral Reflectance Data for Ecological Insights
abstractExcerpt: The massive stream of hyperspectral Earth Observation (EO) data presents huge opportunities for vegetation remote sensing. Recent advances in machine learning and foundational models have demonstrated a remarkable capacity to retrieve plant functional traits directly from spectral reflectance. Field spectroscopy provides the critical link between hyperspectral EO and plant functional traits. It delivers ground reference data on which trait-retrieval models depend.

title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
abstractExcerpt: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood.

abstractExcerpt: Sample preparation increasingly sets the throughput and reproducibility of mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics. StageTips (stop-and-go extraction tips) and variants thereof have long been common implements to purify samples, and we recently extended the concept to solid-phase extraction capture (SPEC) tips, in which the entire digestion takes place in sub-microliter volumes. Here we replace the hand-packed bed with a strong anion-exchange (SAX) monolith photopolymerized directly inside the pipette tip from a defined recipe (pSPEC).

title: Mode-selective electron-phonon coupling drives charge density waves in the kagome metals YRu$_3$Si$_2$ and LaRu$_3$Si$_2$
abstractExcerpt: YRu$_3$Si$_2$ and LaRu$_3$Si$_2$ host the highest charge density wave (CDW) transition temperatures ever reported in kagome metals, $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}\approx 800$ and 400~K, with propagation vectors $Q_{\mathrm{CDW}}\approx(1/2,0,0)$ and $(1/4,0,0)$, respectively. The microscopic mechanism behind these record values has remained unresolved. Here, we combine anharmonic phonon renormalization extracted from molecular dynamics driven by a machine-learned force field with mode-resolved electron-phonon coupling (EPC) analysis to identify this mechanism.
